name: Montco Forever Green Grant Program

funder.name: Montgomery County Planning Commission, Montgomery County, Pennsylvania

summary: County grants for fee-title and conservation-easement purchases of open land in Montgomery County, Pennsylvania. Municipalities and nonprofit land conservation organisations can apply, with a 25 percent minimum match.

eligibility.rule: Is a Montgomery County municipality or qualified nonprofit with a land conservation mission and history
Nonprofits include Montgomery County in their geographic program area
Not an authority, commission, school district, special taxing district, private organization or individual
Acquires land that lacks adequate and perpetual open-space protection
Uses acquired land as open space, not prohibited public-facility or utility uses
Gives some form of public access, unless limits protect sensitive ecological features
Land not yet bought: acquisition costs before the grant award are not funded

status.quote: Timing: Applications accepted on a rolling basis.

applicant_types.quote: Eligible applicants: The County's 62 municipalities and nonprofit land conservation organizations.

geography.quote: Eligible projects: Any open land located in the County with no limitation on size.

window.quote: Timing: Applications accepted on a rolling basis.

co_finance_required.quote: Match requirement: Minimum 25 percent match of grant award.

consortium_required.quote: Applicants may partner with other public agencies, nonprofit organizations, or private entities, but the primary applicant will be responsible for administering the grant.

effort.quote: In coordination with MCPC staff, the applicant provides a project introduction to the OSB at a duly advertised public meeting.
Applicant submits full application including all materials listed above under Application Requirements.
Applications are reviewed by MCPC staff for completeness.

eligibility.quote: All 62 municipalities in Montgomery County are eligible to apply for open space grants as the primary applicant. Additionally, land trusts and other qualified nonprofit organizations that include land conservation as part of their mission and have a history of land conservation are also eligible to apply.
Eligible nonprofit organizations do not need to be headquartered in the county but must include the county as part of their geographic program area.
Entities such as authorities, commissions, school districts, special taxing districts, private organizations, individuals, or other similar entities, are not eligible to apply for these funds.

With the exception of land that already possesses adequate and perpetual protection as open space, as determined by MCPC staff, any land within Montgomery County may be eligible for acquisition as open space under this grant program

Open space purchased under this grant program shall not be used for activities such as municipal building sites, detention basins, public utilities (including cell towers, solar arrays, or wind farms), fire or police stations, public works or maintenance yards, or other similar uses.
Some form of appropriate public access on open space properties acquired with county grant funds is required in most cases.
Land and easement acquisition costs incurred prior to the grant award are not eligible for county grant funding/reimbursement.

documents.quote: Signed Application Letter: For municipal applicants, the letter should be signed by the head of the governing body. For nonprofit organization applicants, the letter should be signed by the president or chair of the organization. 3. Resolution of Authorization: An official resolution authorizing the applicant to submit the application is required.
The Project Narrative shall be no more than six (6) pages in length (single spaced, 12-point type).

Provide map of the municipality showing the exact location of the proposed acquisition; a property or tax map showing the property size, configuration and relationship to abutting properties and a few representative photos of the subject property.
Provide a complete copy of the property appraisal used to establish fair market value.
Provide information outlining anticipated funding sources and amounts, including the grant being requested from the county and the required 25% match.

co_finance.quote: The minimum project match must be at least 25% of the grant award (e.g., a $100,000 grant request will require a $25,000 match).
